messages.content: Act as a skeptical ICLR area chair and world-model security researcher. Strictly review the candidate below, score actual publishable novelty, and return JSON only. Reject rebranding of generic LoRA merging, model supply-chain backdoors, multi-task interference, or rollout error.

{"candidate": {"title": "Adapter-composition integrity failure in latent dynamics", "one_sentence_claim": "World-model adapters that are individually safe and one-step validated can become jointly unsafe when composed, because cross-terms between low-rank updates to the recurrent latent transition create a physically inconsistent counterfactual geometry that only appears under closed-loop planning.", "attacker": "A tenant can submit a legitimate task adapter to a shared world-model service; it passes isolated holdout replay and standalone task checks, but the router later merges it with another tenant adapter. No base-weight, gradient, label, or impossible-state access.", "mechanism": "For nonlinear recurrent dynamics, composing parameter updates is not equivalent to composing their induced transition operators: mixed Jacobian/Hessian terms alter action-conditioned reachability only in joint adapter subspaces. Pointwise one-step metrics and isolated adapter evaluations cannot observe the mixed term; CEM/actor planning can select the resulting false reachability.", "carrier": "public DreamerV3/TD-MPC2 or a released robot video world model with LoRA/adapter fine-tuning; faithful low-rank latent-dynamics toy as <=90-minute gate.", "repair": "Validate every proposed adapter against pairwise/combinatorial composition tests in latent transition and task rollouts, or constrain adapter subspaces to be orthogonal in the dynamics Jacobian."}, "known_prior": ["generic LoRA/adapters merging and task arithmetic", "supply-chain/checkpoint backdoors in RL/world models", "multi-task negative transfer and interference", "SWAAP/TRAP/BadWAM", "noncommuting update operators and latent geometry screens already in this project", "ordinary rollout compounding and action encoding"], "questions": ["Is the mixed latent-transition operator mechanism genuinely distinct and broad enough for novelty >=7?", "Does it create a security failure beyond generic adapter merge damage?", "What exact short pilot with public carrier and strong controls would decide it, and what falsifies it?", "If rejected, provide at most one alternative."], "fields": ["verdict", "novelty_score", "distinctness", "fatal_flaws", "short_pilot", "repair_assessment", "alternative"]}
